system.summary: Numerical syllable-and-word code (the = 1385), about 1,600 numbers; 1-100 mostly whole words; values climb alphabetically only in short runs, then break; superscript o = plural, a mark under a group modifies it.
system.sibling_key: Armstrong's THE=972 code (targets/armstrong/), which Madison's editors said JQA used; tested and ruled out. Pinkney's London code named in Smith's 1809 instructions (Ford 3:327-28) not tested.
system.notes: distinct_symbols = numbers in code_table.tsv (22 Sept 2026: 391 H, 241 C, 311 M, 19 I), built by consolidate.py from pairs_jqa.txt, clerk_*.tsv (interlinear decodes on frames 0048, 0182, 0183, 0184, 0185, 0189, 0190, 0194, 0198, 0206), ford_pairs*.tsv (39 coded 1811 blocks aligned with Ford vol. 4) and slot_inferences.tsv. Homophones: several words have two groups (those 551/651, English 1291/1292, with 1190/1192-era variants, few 329/350). separation is as transcribed; the manuscript uses dots and spaces.

prior_solution.where: Ford printed both No. 88 passages as not decyphered; the clerk's decode on frame 0206 covers only the rest of the despatch. No other reading found. Ford vol. 4 prints the Department's decipherments of OTHER 1811 despatches in the same code; those were used as known plaintext to rebuild the code (22 Sept 2026), not as a reading of No. 88.

solution.what: Checked the Madison editors' claim that JQA used Armstrong's THE=972 code against Ford 3:327-28 and 3:370.
Fetched NARA M35 reels 2 and 3 frames and scored them for code texture (codescore.py).
Applied the 592-entry Armstrong THE=972 table to JQA's 1812 despatches: noise; his code has the = 1385, of = 1576.
Read the clerk's interlinear decodes on frames 0206 and 0189 into pairs_jqa.txt (262 clerk-attested pairs).
Worked out the code's structure: alphabetical blocks of about 50 numbers, shuffled, whole words in 1-100.
Filled groups by slot inference inside the blocks and context (48 I and 93 M pairs).
Ford's nine undecyphered lines (gap88.txt) read 124 of 134 groups: Rumyantsev's strokes at Wilna and the false report of his death.
The remainder on frame 0207 (rem88.txt) renders 212 of 250 complete groups, in threads only.

Located the images of NARA M35 reel 3 in the main checkout (img03, downloaded 18 Sept) and surveyed the contact sheets: interlinear clerk decodes on frames 0048, 0182-0185, 0190, 0194, 0198, 0211 and later; 'decyphered' sheets for 1811 despatches (0011, 0037, 0064, 0067, 0072, 0082, 0092, ...).

Read the clerk's interlinear decodes on frames 0182 (No. 80, 29 Feb 1812) and 0048 (top) by hand, and on 0183R, 0184, 0185, 0190, 0194R, 0198R with two transcription agents: ~2,000 pairs (1,296 H, 869 M) in clerk_*.tsv.

Transcribed 39 coded blocks of 1811 despatches (frames 0005-0132) and aligned them with the plaintext Ford printed from the Department's decipherments (Writings vol. 4) using align.py, checked by eye: 589 C and 270 M pairs in ford_pairs*.tsv.
Merged all sources into one table (consolidate.py, overrides.tsv for 40 disputed numbers): 962 numbers, 391 H, 241 C, 311 M, 19 I. The alphabetical order holds only in short runs.
Re-read the No. 88 groups from zoomed crops of frames 0206 and 0207: three digits corrected (168, 1426, 302) and a catchword (1102) removed; 1081 in the remainder line 5 is blurred.

Alphabetical-slot bracketing of the groups still unread (slots.py): nine grade-I values (168 ey, 1434 journ, 83 opposition, 143 mod, 815 def, 239 sive, 108 comply, 432 net, 726 rate); 1575 and 1540, first slot-inferred as off and along, were then attested by Ford as adv and ambass.

No. 88 re-measured with measure.py and a sense-flag file (sense88.tsv): 379 of 390 groups valued, 355 read as sense (0.910); Ford's nine lines 127/133 (0.955), the remainder 228/257 (0.887). Before this session: 336 of 391 valued (0.859), sense not measured.

Clerk interlinear decodes read on frames 0047, 0048 (rest), 0210-0211, 0247 (560 pairs; clerk_0047.tsv etc.); 0056-57 found to be a clear decyphered copy of No. 46; 220 = probab (three clerk readings) replaces proper.

Coded blocks of eight despatches Oct 1811-Sept 1812 transcribed and aligned with Ford vol. 4; No. 95 aligned against the Department's clear copy on 0230-0232 (1,926 pairs; ford1812_pairs*.tsv): 996 = fri (friendship), 1457+ = ll (Chancellor), 83 = opposition, 1061 = cu, 588 = tled.

No. 88 re-read on zoomed crops of 0206R and 0207: 792 not 492 (by), 1061 not 1081 (e-va-cu-ation), 588 not 888 (bat-tle), 1384 not 1385 (that); 570 and 1099 confirmed; the 7 line-end groups are cut by the binding gutter.

Alphabetical-slot inferences (grade I) for the remaining groups: 1403 ib and 350 fl (in-fl-ex-ib-ly, inflexibly), 1309 bat (battle of Friedland), 426 negotiate, 1540 along; 927 pire from context only.
measure.py: 375 of 390 groups read as sense (0.962), gap88 0.970, rem88 0.957; open: 7 gutter-cut groups, im-pas-sion-ed (JQA slip for impaired), 1508, 1185, 570, 748.
rem88 l.19 re-read: 1097 sho (last digit overwritten 9->7) and 1383 than (5/3 overwritten), both M: "than along the sho-res of the Baltic"; 748 res now reads. 376/390 = 0.964.

Five more 1811-1812 despatches aligned with Ford (Nos. 71, 72, 74, 75, 81; ford1812_pairs_b.tsv): JQA's own 'un-im-pa-ir-ed' in No. 83 (1477 1424 1102 1435 520) and his catchword 1102 show that No. 88's 1112 1433 are copying slips; the phrase reads 'had not been impaired'. 1185, 1508 not found; 570 = tol(d) confirmed four more times.
measure.py: 380 of 390 groups read as sense (0.974): gap88 133/133, rem88 247/257; open: 7 gutter-cut groups (needs the original), 1508, 1185, 570.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 380 tokens, 207 types, en-modern order 4: reading -1.962 per letter; random keys -2.897 (z 9.0); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -1.989 (mean -2.005, z 3.5); annealer on the real text -2.002. Verdict: pass.

Page split under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): No. 88, in Adams's own St Petersburg code (the = 1385), had shared the page legation.html with Erving's 1807 letter in Pinckney's code (the = 1651); it now has its own page jqa.html, card, badge and credits line. Profile content unchanged.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): gap88.txt and rem88.txt; the readings copied from NOTES.md sections 3-4 with render.py output into texts/no88_*_decryption.md; key code_table.tsv.

Verification 5 (plain-bar rows): both No. 88 entries had been scored on decryption files with hyphenated syllables and group tables (the gap entry listed as French). Readings written out with words joined (texts/no88_gap_reading.md, no88_remainder_reading.md): plain 0.9 and 0.688, explicit 1.0 and 0.812. Both keep read.

texts.label: No. 88, 25 June 1812: the nine lines Ford did not decipher
texts.summary: John Quincy Adams at St Petersburg to the Secretary of State, the day after Napoleon crossed the Niemen: Chancellor Rumyantsev opposed Alexander's journey to Wilna, suffered an apoplectic stroke soon after arriving and a second, worse one since; a German report of his death was false, and JQA judges he cannot long remain at the foreign ministry.

reading_review.note: v5 check 23 Oct 2026: listed as French; the despatch is English (1812), so the plain share is a bar too. The sweep scored the decryption file with its hyphenated syllables and group table (plain 0.192, explicit 0.808). Reading written out with words joined, grade-I words marked, texts/no88_gap_reading.md: plain 0.9 (9/10), explicit 1.0. Keeps read.

texts.label: No. 88, 25 June 1812: the remainder Ford printed as undecyphered (frame 0207)
texts.summary: The rest of No. 88: a proposal to evacuate Prussia as a preliminary to negotiation would have been neither unreasonable nor offensive; the French ambassador Lauriston took Prince Kurakin's note as proof that Alexander would not negotiate; and JQA expects that early French success would let Napoleon strike directly at the centre of the empire rather than along the Baltic.

texts.label: Everett to Clay, Madrid, 25 Sep 1825 (catalogue 638), M31 reel 27 frames 0119-0121
texts.summary: Everett's notes of a conversation with the foreign minister Zea Bermudez on recognising the new American states: Zea's refusal is a language imposed on him by circumstances; the foreign ministers think him privately favourable but unable to risk his place against his rivals; the influence of Emperor Alexander is directed against recognition, and Russia's policy is put down to opposition to England rather than to legitimacy.

reading_review.by: WAINUT (AI language-model agent, checked against the frames)
reading_review.note: Coherent sentences; 23 holes in about 240 words: 8 open groups and 15 context-only or against-the-table words, all marked [?]. read_share = 1 - hole rate of docs/_check_reading.py --file (0.096).

texts.label: Crawford to Monroe, No. 1 (private), Paris, 3 Sept 1813 (catalogue 652), M34 roll 17 frames 0027R-0029R
texts.summary: The new US minister in Paris explains why he has not opened official talks with Napoleon's foreign minister Bassano, who is with the Emperor at Dresden: Mr. Warden acts as the channel at Paris, a minister need not follow a court abroad, and Crawford has been painted as impetuous; the Russian mediation is unwelcome to Napoleon. He then judges Joel Barlow's secret plan to fund indemnities from trade licences useless, since licensed imports have glutted the American market.

reading_review.by: WAINUT (AI language-model agent, checked against the frames)
reading_review.note: Coherent sentences with scattered holes: about 40 context words marked [?] and about 30 open groups; 1264 read as the full stop (from 653). research/reading_audit/v2_score.py: hole rate 0.084, explicit-hole sentence share 0.732; docs/_check_reading.py clean share 0.69. Under the 95% bar, so read in part.

texts.label: Ellis to Forsyth, No. 9, Mexico, 16 Nov 1839 (catalogue 653), M97 roll 10 frames 0298-0303
texts.summary: The US minister in Mexico reports that Texian troops with disaffected Mexicans have crossed the line, apparently to attack Matamoros, and that the government is sending General Arista to the frontier with 4,000 men; a war with Texas would unite the Mexican parties; the foreign minister Cañedo wants a general congress of the Spanish American states, unlikely to succeed. The Department's 1839 clear copy is in the same file.

reading_review.by: WAINUT (AI language-model agent, checked against the frames and the 1839 clear copy)
reading_review.note: Every group lines up with a word or syllable of the contemporary clear copy (frames 0300-0301); values missing from the table are taken from it. v2_score.py: hole rate 0.0. Two groups are illegible on the film; their words rest on the clear copy.
